## Overview

My research lies at the intersection of **Gravitational Wave (GW) Astrophysics** and **Cosmology**. I focus on developing and applying statistical methods — in particular beyond-Gaussian parameter estimation techniques — to extract cosmological and astrophysical information from GW observations with current and next-generation detectors.

---

## Research Areas

### Cosmology with Gravitational Waves

Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) provide a direct, independent measurement of luminosity distance, making them powerful **standard sirens** for cosmology. My work explores how third-generation (3G) detectors such as the **Einstein Telescope** and **Cosmic Explorer** can constrain cosmological parameters — including the Hubble constant $H_0$ and dark energy models — using both bright (electromagnetic-counterpart) and dark sirens (statistical methods with galaxy catalogs).

### Parameter Estimation Beyond the Gaussian Approximation

The standard Fisher-matrix approach to GW parameter estimation assumes Gaussian posteriors, which breaks down at low signal-to-noise ratio or for non-linear signal models. I develop and apply the **Derivative Approximation for Likelihoods (DALI)**, a higher-order expansion that captures non-Gaussian features of the posterior at low computational cost. DALI is implemented in [**GWDALI**](https://pypi.org/project/gwdali/), an open-source Python package I developed and maintain.

### Third-Generation Gravitational Wave Observatories

I study the science potential of next-generation GW observatories, contributing to the **Einstein Telescope** collaboration through the ET Observational Science Board (ET-OSB). My contributions span cosmology forecasts, detector network optimization, and gravitational-wave data analysis pipelines.

### Numerical Modeling & High-Performance Computing

A significant part of my work involves large-scale numerical simulations of GW source populations and Monte Carlo parameter estimation. I make extensive use of Python, C, and parallel computing on HPC clusters.

## Research Groups & Memberships

### Núcleo Cosmo-UFES & PPGCosmo
Postdoctoral Fellow (since Oct. 2025) at the Cosmology group of the Universidade Federal do Espírito Santo, funded by FAPES. Working on gravitational-wave cosmology and DALI-based inference.

Member since June 2022. Active contributor to:

Member since January 2024. Contribution: improvements on the DALI approximation for GW data analysis and cosmology.

## Software

### GWDALI
An open-source Python package (available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/gwdali/)) implementing the **Derivative Approximation for Likelihoods (DALI)** for GW parameter estimation beyond the Gaussian approximation, in user-defined detector networks.

```bash
pip install gwdali
```
